name: California
tagline: Big Sur cliffs, Sierra passes, Death Valley sinks and the levee roads of the Delta.
intro: California's scenic highways run from the Big Sur and Gaviota coasts over the Sierra passes at Ebbetts, Carson and Monitor, through the Owens Valley and Death Valley, and along freeways and levee roads around the Bay Area and the Delta. This chapter follows the State Scenic Highway Program, created by the Legislature in 1963 and run by the California Department of Transportation (Caltrans), whose officially designated route segments are grouped here into 48 roads; the many highways that are only "eligible" are left out. Caltrans designates stretches of numbered routes by postmile rather than naming byways, so most roads here go by their route number, and national forest, BLM and national byways that the state never designated are listed separately.

programs.label: California State Scenic Highway System (officially designated)

members.name: Route 1, San Mateo County
members.blurb: Highway 1 runs twenty-six miles up the San Mateo coast from the Santa Cruz County line to Half Moon Bay, passing the marine mammal colonies at Año Nuevo State Park and the old lighthouse at Pigeon Point.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 1, Big Sur Coast (Monterey County)
members.blurb: Highway 1 clings to the Big Sur cliffs for some seventy miles between San Carpóforo Creek and the Carmel River, crossing the concrete arch of Bixby Bridge. In 1965 it became the first road California named a scenic highway.

members.name: Route 1, San Luis Obispo North Coast
members.blurb: Highway 1 leaves San Luis Obispo for the north coast, running through Cambria and San Simeon, past the turnoff for Hearst Castle and the elephant seals hauled out near the Piedras Blancas light station.

members.name: Route 1, Santa Barbara County (Las Cruces to Lompoc)
members.blurb: Eighteen miles of the Cabrillo Highway, where Highway 1 parts from US 101 at Las Cruces and heads northwest toward Lompoc. Las Cruces itself disappeared under the highway interchange built there in 1967.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 2, Angeles Crest Highway
members.blurb: The Angeles Crest Highway climbs out of La Cañada Flintridge into the San Gabriel Mountains and tops out near 7,900 feet at Dawson Saddle. Snow usually shuts the stretch between Islip Saddle and Vincent Gap through winter.
members.note: Shown on the map as Angeles Crest Scenic Byway (Route 2).

members.name: Route 4, Ebbetts Pass
members.blurb: East of Arnold, Highway 4 climbs past the Bear Valley turnoff and narrows to a single lane with no center line on its way over 8,730-foot Ebbetts Pass, which is left unplowed and closes for the winter.

members.name: Routes 5 and 580, West Side Freeway
members.blurb: Interstate 5 runs north along the foot of the Diablo Range on the west edge of the San Joaquin Valley, crossing and recrossing the California Aqueduct, and I-580 carries the designation on toward Altamont.

members.name: Route 9, Saratoga-Los Gatos Road
members.blurb: Highway 9 descends seven miles from Saratoga Gap on the crest of the Santa Cruz Mountains to Saratoga village, a grade cyclists crowd on weekend mornings, then runs on as Saratoga-Los Gatos Road toward Los Gatos.

members.name: Route 12, Valley of the Moon (Sonoma County)
members.blurb: Highway 12 leaves the east side of Santa Rosa and turns south into the Sonoma Valley, the Valley of the Moon, passing Jack London State Historic Park at Glen Ellen before ending near Agua Caliente.

members.name: Route 20, Nevada County
members.blurb: Six and a half miles of Highway 20 on the ridges east of Nevada City, near Skillman Flat, where the Pioneer Trail follows beside the road on part of an 1850 branch of the California Trail.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 24, Contra Costa County
members.blurb: Highway 24 comes out of the Caldecott Tunnel's east portal and runs through the wooded hills of Orinda and Lafayette to Walnut Creek, with BART trains running in the median much of the way.
members.note: Shown on the map as Route 24--Alameda County.

members.name: Route 27, Topanga Canyon Boulevard
members.blurb: Two and a half miles of Topanga Canyon Boulevard, starting a mile up from the Pacific Coast Highway, where the road winds up the canyon into the Santa Monica Mountains. Caltrans designated it in 2017.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 33, Maricopa Highway (Ventura County)
members.blurb: North of Ojai, Highway 33 follows Matilija Canyon into Los Padres National Forest and climbs over Pine Mountain Summit, on a route the Reyes family laid out to reach the coast from their Cuyama ranch.
members.note: Shown on the map as Jacinto Reyes Scenic Byway (Route 33).

members.name: Route 35, Skyline Boulevard
members.blurb: Skyline Boulevard keeps to the crest of the Santa Cruz Mountains for some twenty-three miles through San Mateo County, past the crossroads hamlet of Sky Londa, to its junction with Highway 92.

members.name: Route 38, San Bernardino Mountains
members.blurb: Fifteen miles of Highway 38 in the San Bernardino Mountains, climbing from the South Fork campground over Onyx Summit at 8,443 feet, among the highest pavement in southern California, and down toward Big Bear.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 49, Sierra County
members.blurb: Highway 49 runs forty-one miles through the forests of Sierra County, from the Yuba County line through the gold-rush towns of Downieville and Sierra City and up to Yuba Summit.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 50, El Dorado County
members.blurb: US 50 climbs from Placerville up the canyon of the South Fork of the American River, through Kyburz and the hairpins above Strawberry to Echo Summit, then drops to Lake Tahoe along an old Pony Express corridor.

members.name: Route 52, Mission Trails
members.blurb: Three and a half miles of the SR 52 freeway across Mission Trails Regional Park in San Diego, climbing over Mission Trails Pass below Fortuna Mountain with a bicycle path running alongside. Caltrans designated it in 2016.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 62, Twentynine Palms Highway
members.blurb: Nine miles of Twentynine Palms Highway, leaving Interstate 10 at the eastern end of San Gorgonio Pass near Whitewater and running north toward Morongo Valley and the San Bernardino County line.

members.name: Route 68, Monterey-Salinas Highway
members.blurb: The Monterey-Salinas Highway runs fourteen miles inland from Highway 1 to the Salinas River, through chaparral hills with lupine in spring, past the Laguna Seca raceway and the turnoff up Laureles Grade.
members.note: Shown on the map as Route 68--Monterey County.

members.name: Routes 74 and 243, Palms to Pines
members.blurb: Highway 74 climbs from Palm Desert by Deep Canyon through Pinyon Pines and Garner Valley to Mountain Center, where Highway 243 turns north through Idyllwild and switchbacks down to Banning.

members.name: Route 75, Silver Strand and Coronado Bridge
members.blurb: Highway 75 runs up the Silver Strand, a thin spit between the Pacific and San Diego Bay, through Coronado and onto the Coronado bridge, which curves eighty degrees and rises high enough for Navy ships.
members.note: Shown on the map as Route 75--San Diego-Coronado Bridge and Silver Strand Highway.

members.name: Route 78, Anza-Borrego Desert State Park
members.blurb: Below Julian and the old Banner toll road, Highway 78 passes Scissors Crossing and runs eighteen miles across Anza-Borrego Desert State Park to Ocotillo Wells.

members.name: Route 84, Niles Canyon Road
members.blurb: Niles Canyon Road follows Alameda Creek between Sunol and the Niles district of Fremont, with the Niles Canyon Railway running on the old Southern Pacific line and a silent-film studio's old back lot at the western mouth.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 88, Carson Pass Highway
members.blurb: Highway 88 climbs past Kirkwood and Caples Lake to Carson Pass on an old emigrant trail route, then drops by Red Lake into Hope Valley and down Woodfords Canyon toward Nevada.
members.note: Shown on the map as Carson Pass Highway (Route 88).

members.name: Route 89, Monitor Pass, Luther Pass and Lake Tahoe
members.blurb: Highway 89 climbs over Monitor Pass at 8,314 feet, drops to the Carson River at Markleeville and Woodfords, crosses Luther Pass and follows Lake Tahoe's west shore past Emerald Bay.
members.note: Shown on the map as Route 89--Monitor Pass & Luther Pass Highways & Lake Tahoe Road.

members.name: Route 91, Riverside Freeway (Orange County)
members.blurb: About four miles of the Riverside Freeway in Orange County, from Highway 55 east to the Anaheim city limit, where the freeway enters the western end of the Santa Ana Canyon.

members.name: Route 101, Del Norte Coast Redwoods
members.blurb: Twelve miles of US 101 through Del Norte Coast Redwoods State Park, where the highway works across Last Chance Grade, a stretch Caltrans has proposed bypassing by tunnel, on its way north to Crescent City.
members.note: Shown on the map as Route 101--Redwood Highway.

members.name: Route 101, Gaviota Coast
members.blurb: US 101 follows the Gaviota Coast west of Goleta for about nineteen miles, past the beaches at El Capitán and Refugio, then turns inland through Gaviota Pass, where only northbound traffic takes the tunnel.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 116, Sonoma County
members.blurb: Highway 116 leaves the coast near Jenner and follows the north bank of the Russian River through Monte Rio and Guerneville, then cuts through Pocket Canyon to Forestville and runs down the Gravenstein Highway to Sebastopol.

members.name: Route 125, La Mesa
members.blurb: Not quite two miles of the SR 125 freeway between Highway 94 and Interstate 8 at La Mesa, a stretch the city of La Mesa first proposed for scenic designation in 1968.
members.note: Shown on the map as Route 125--Lemon Grove.

members.name: Route 140, Mariposa County
members.blurb: Highway 140 leaves Mariposa through the ponderosa pines of Midpines, drops to Briceburg and follows the Merced River canyon on the 1926 All-Year Highway, with the old Yosemite Valley Railroad line once running along the far bank.

members.name: Route 151, Shasta Dam Boulevard
members.blurb: Shasta Dam Boulevard runs three miles south from the visitor center below Shasta Dam, a 602-foot wall holding back the largest reservoir in California, through thick green country toward Lake Boulevard.

members.name: Route 152, Pacheco Pass Road (Merced County)
members.blurb: From the Santa Clara County line below Pacheco Pass, once a Butterfield stage stop, Highway 152 descends the Diablo Range along San Luis Reservoir, between the dam and the O'Neill Forebay, to Interstate 5.

members.name: Route 154, San Marcos Pass Road
members.blurb: Highway 154, the Chumash Highway, leaves Los Olivos past Lake Cachuma and crosses the Santa Ynez Mountains at San Marcos Pass, high over Cold Spring Canyon, where an old tavern sits on the stage road below.

members.name: Route 156, Castroville to Prunedale
members.blurb: About four miles of two-lane Highway 156 from the edge of Castroville, the town that calls itself the Artichoke Center of the World, east to US 101 at Prunedale.
members.note: Shown on the map as Route 156--Monterey County.

members.name: Route 160, Sacramento River Delta
members.blurb: Highway 160 rides the Sacramento River levees through the Delta to the edge of Sacramento, crossing the river on 1920s drawbridges at Isleton and Paintersville, on what boosters once called the Netherlands Route.
members.note: Shown on the map as Route 160--River Road.

members.name: Route 163, Cabrillo Freeway through Balboa Park
members.blurb: The Cabrillo Freeway's run through Balboa Park, opened in 1948 as San Diego County's first freeway, is built like a parkway, with a wide grassy median planted with trees and tight curves under the Cabrillo Bridge.

members.name: Route 168, Bishop Creek
members.blurb: Highway 168 climbs about sixteen miles from Bishop up the Bishop Creek country to Lake Sabrina, a reservoir dammed in 1907 to run power plants. The top stretch above Aspendell closes to most traffic in winter.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 180, Kings Canyon
members.blurb: Highway 180 climbs out of the San Joaquin Valley through the General Grant Grove of giant sequoias, then descends 2,700 feet into the canyon of the Kings River and ends just past Cedar Grove.

members.name: Route 190, Death Valley
members.blurb: Highway 190 crosses Death Valley National Park from the Panamint Valley over Towne Pass to Stovepipe Wells and Furnace Creek, then climbs Furnace Creek Wash, roughly the trail the Death Valley '49ers came in by in 1849.

members.name: Route 247, High Desert (Barstow to Yucca Valley)
members.blurb: Highway 247 crosses the high desert between Yucca Valley and Barstow on Old Woman Springs Road, past Joshua trees, Black Lava Butte and the flat of Lucerne Dry Lake. Designated in 2025.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 280, Junipero Serra Freeway
members.blurb: Interstate 280 runs up the San Mateo County hills along the San Andreas rift, above Crystal Springs Reservoir, on a stretch dedicated as the World's Most Beautiful Freeway.
members.note: Shown on the map as Route 280--Father Junipero Serra Freeway.

members.name: Route 395, Inyo County
members.blurb: Nineteen miles of US 395 up the Owens Valley from the Fort Independence reservation, past Tinemaha Reservoir and the spot where the Los Angeles Aqueduct draws from the Owens River, toward Big Pine.

members.name: Route 395, Mono County
members.blurb: US 395 crosses nearly all of Mono County, from Crowley Lake over Deadman Summit to Mono Lake at Lee Vining, then over Conway Summit and Devil's Gate and down the West Walker River.

members.name: Route 580, MacArthur Freeway (Oakland)
members.blurb: The MacArthur Freeway runs ten miles through Oakland from the San Leandro line to the Highway 24 junction, finished in 1966 and still closed to heavy trucks through the city.

members.name: Route 680, Alameda County
members.blurb: Interstate 680 climbs from Mission Boulevard in Fremont over the Sunol Grade into the Sunol Valley and on north past Pleasanton.

members.name: Route 680, Contra Costa County
members.blurb: Fourteen miles of Interstate 680 up the San Ramon Valley along the line of the Calaveras Fault, past Danville and Alamo to the Highway 24 junction at Walnut Creek.

members.name: Laureles Grade Road
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: River Road (Sacramento County)
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Interlake Road (Lockwood to the San Luis Obispo County line)
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Interlake Road and Nacimiento Drive
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Lake Boulevard (County Road A-18)
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Malibu Canyon-Las Virgenes Highway (N1)
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Mulholland Highway
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

programs.label: National Scenic Byways and All-American Roads

members.name: Arroyo Seco Historic Parkway (Route 110)
members.blurb: The Arroyo Seco Parkway, mostly opened in 1940 beside the Arroyo Seco between downtown Los Angeles and Pasadena, is one of the oldest freeways in the country and is now on the National Register of Historic Places.

members.name: Tioga Road / Big Oak Flat Road
members.blurb: The Tioga Road crosses Yosemite's high country past Tuolumne Meadows to Tioga Pass at 9,945 feet, the highest highway pass in California. In heavy snow years it has stayed closed into late July.

members.name: Volcanic Legacy Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A five-hundred-mile All-American Road that strings together the volcanoes of the far north, from Lassen Volcanic National Park past Mount Shasta and Medicine Lake to Crater Lake in Oregon.

members.name: Ancient Bristlecone Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A climb from the Owens Valley into the dry White Mountains to Schulman Grove, where bristlecone pines more than four thousand years old stand above views of the Great Basin. The nearest fuel is back in Big Pine.

members.name: Bigfoot Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 96 follows the Klamath River downstream from Happy Camp to Orleans, one of three scenic byways the Forest Service lists through the Klamath National Forest.

members.name: Modoc Volcanic Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Out of McCloud on Highway 89 and northeast to Medicine Lake, through volcanic country where snow closes the road to everything but snowmobiles from about November.

members.name: Rim of the World Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A 110-mile route along the rim of the San Bernardino Mountains from Cajon Pass to San Gorgonio Pass on Highways 138, 18 and 38, open all year though chains are sometimes needed.

members.name: Sierra Heritage Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 168 climbs seventy miles from Clovis up the western slope of the Sierra Nevada, past resort towns and lakes, to Kaiser Pass Meadow at about nine thousand feet.

members.name: Sierra Vista Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A hundred miles of forest roads through the Sierra National Forest, beginning near North Fork and ending near Oakhurst, a drive the Forest Service reckons at about five hours.

members.name: State of Jefferson Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 96 runs up the Klamath River from Pioneer Bridge to Happy Camp, where the byway turns off onto Greyback Road and crosses to O'Brien, Oregon, on US 199.

members.name: Sunrise Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The Sunrise Highway, built in 1937, runs through the pines and meadows of the Laguna Mountains, past a 1912 log ranger cabin and a picnic area looking down six thousand feet to the desert.

members.name: Trinity Heritage Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From the old mining town of Weaverville north to Interstate 5 near Weed, with a free self-guided brochure from the Weaverville ranger station that marks seventeen stops along the way.

members.name: Trinity Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 299 west from Shasta, outside Redding, over the mountains to Blue Lake near Arcata, a route the Forest Service themed From the Valley Oaks to the Redwood Coast when it was designated in 1991.
